messages:
alex: Heads-up — ACME reported a sharp p99 spike (~2.2s -> ~6.9s) on /v1/generate after we onboarded crane-v1 and the tokenizer tweak this morning. also seeing a handful of 401s intermingled with the latency hits.
maya: Which rollout batch and config? full or canary?
alex: Full rollout at 09:12 PT. tokenizer change = normalize_unicode_v3 + bpe-merge tweak. customer calls started showing issues ~09:35.
jean: (support-bot) Ticket #82741 opened for ACME — assigned to alex.
jordan: Do we have traces? p99 across which model sizes? crane-v1-small/med/large?
alex: Attached traces show most tails on crane-v1-large. p95 smaller bump. spans show long time in "runtime:dispatch" before the first token.
kai: We saw similar before when token counts jumped — tokenizer normalization can explode sequence length for some inputs (especially CJK + emoji). any payload samples?
alex: Sending sample payloads in DM. quick summary: token count went up ~1.6x for many requests. example: input len 1800 chars -> tokens 2100 -> after change tokens 3350.
rory: Also spotted ~0.3% 401s originating from auth-service returning intermittent 401s during the same window — maybe unrelated but concurrent. billing/quotas also reported transient 429s from our side.
zuri: Looking at infra: GPU kernels chosen changed because effective seq_len distribution increased — that can push runtime into slower attention kernel path. pairing with larger batch windows = higher latency.
maya: Quick repro steps for eng-runtime: curl the same prompt set with crane-v1-large, with client token, set "max_tokens": 512, track timings. example curl: ```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"crane-v1-large","input":"<sample>","max_tokens":512}' | jq .
```
jordan: I can reproduce locally on canary — p99 ~6.8s. reverting tokenizer to previous normalization stops the blowup (tokens back to ~2080).
alex: Customer is asking for ETA and mitigation. what immediate mitigations can we offer?
kai: Options: 1) Roll back tokenizer perf patch (fast) 2) Pin ACME to crane-v1@revA (older tokenizer) via routing override (quicker, targeted) 3) Enable stricter token-length capping on gateway for this tenant while we investigate (risk: truncation)
eve: From CS: ACME prefers not to be truncated; they want minimal correctness impact. they asked for a routing pin to older model if possible.
rory: I can do a per-tenant route pin for ACME to crane-v1@revA now, and open a rollback PR for the tokenizer change.
deploy-bot: (deploy-bot) Routing change request #r-994 submitted by rory — awaiting approval.
alex: Also need a mitigation for the 401s — looks like auth-service had a short GC pause coincident with rollout. zuri, can you confirm auth logs?
zuri: Confirmed: auth-service pod restarted once at 09:31 due to OOM from an unrelated leak. restart caused ~120s window of transient 401s. I've put a hotfix to increase memory and restarted replicas.
jordan: After routing pin, p99 for ACME drops back to ~2.4s. platform-wide customers still show a mild bump — likely other tenants with heavy CJK traffic hit the same.
maya: Next steps: 1) Apply per-tenant pin for high-risk customers (rory) 2) Rollback tokenizer patch (rollback PR in flight) 3) Engineering to analyze kernel selection thresholds and add a safety-fallback to preserve lower-latency kernels when token count increases modestly (eng-runtime).
kai: For longer-term: add preflight token-penalty estimation during onboarding and flag token inflation >1.25x to require manual review. also add a canary that simulates corner-case CJK+emoji traffic.
alex: I've notified ACME CS and offered routing pin + status update. CS wants ETA for rollback (how long?).
rory: Routing pin now in prod (r-994 applied). rollback PR drafted, CI running — if green, I can merge and canary deploy in ~30m, full rollback in ~2h.
eve: ACME accepted routing pin and asked to be notified when rollback completes.
zuri: Auth hotfix deployed; error rate back to baseline.
jordan: Follow-up: collecting histogram of token inflation by model shard to detect other vulnerable models. will post results in this thread.
alex: Thanks all. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml to prioritize kernel-safety changes. I'll update ACME in 15m. :thumbsup:
